description: Gifted-K (age 5, pre-reader) curiosity thread — same behaviors as the k-bug-legs spot script: breathless run-ons, invented spelling, a mid-thread topic hop (bugs → worms), and an 'i dont know' stall. The authored assistant turns are the healthy K register (plan §5): 1–3 short sentences, one idea and one question per turn, NO markdown/bullets/headers, physical + think-aloud probes, an offered image, warmth about the THINKING not the child, a gentle bridge back after the hop — the reasoning stays hers. In --mode regenerate against the current (pre-P0, register-less) prompt, the dimensions that catch adult-register drift are ageFit (should crater on stacked questions / big words / long turns read aloud to a 5-year-old), didacticDensity (info-dumping the six-legs answer), socratic/overScaffolding (answer-dumping vs. handing back), and onTask (chasing the worm hop instead of honoring-then-bridging).

turns.content: Hi Posy. Bugs today. What made you start wondering about their legs?
why do bugs have six legs why not like a hundred legs
Six is a funny number, huh. Try this with me. Stand up and lift one foot. Are you wobbly?
i counted a ant one time. one two three... it had six i counted all of them
Six, and you counted every one. That's careful looking. So when you stood on one foot, what did your body do?
That's okay. When I get stuck, I try it small. Put just one finger down on the table. Can one finger hold up a whole book?
OH WAIT do worms have legs. becuz i digged one up in the yard and it was all squishy and it had NO legs not even one leg
Ooh, a worm with no legs at all. Want me to draw one so we can look?
worms dont got bones thats why there squishy. i got bones look i can feel them right here on my arm
You figured that out yourself. Squishy because no bones. So back to your bug. What do you think six feet help it do?
wait but why do the bugs need six tho. thats what i wanna know
